chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-'Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said:

I asked him about a man who had children and he married off two of them and specified the dowry (sadaq), then he died. From where is the dowry accounted for: from the total wealth or from their share? He said: 'From all the wealth, for it is in the position of a debt.'

key_terms.الصَّدَاق: Dowry or bridal price specified in marriage contract
key_terms.بِمَنْزِلَةِ الدَّيْنِ: In the position/status of a debt
key_terms.جُمْلَةِ الْمَالِ: The total wealth/estate of the deceased

ai.seo_question: How is a father's obligation to pay dowry for his children handled upon his death in Shia inheritance law?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, the Imam clarifies that the dowry (sadaq) for multiple daughters is treated as a consolidated debt against the entire estate rather than being apportioned strictly to their specific shares. This ruling ensures that creditors, including the dowry obligation, are settled prior to the distribution of inheritance, reflecting the principle that *sadaq* holds the legal status of a debt (*dayn*). This distinction is crucial in Shia jurisprudence for determining the correct order of financial settlements upon death.
